question: How does an octopus retune its nerve proteins when its water turns cold?
answer: By editing its RNA, the working copies of genes, while the DNA stays unchanged. California two-spot octopuses kept at 13 °C instead of 22 °C raised protein-altering edits at more than 13,000 sites in the nervous system within days. The same gene then yields slightly different proteins: a winter wardrobe from the same pattern.
move: A fixed blueprint can still yield different products if the copies change.
ask: If who I am stays the same, what around me is changing what comes out?
source: Birk et al., Cell, 2023; Marine Biological Laboratory
